subject: Human Evolution
title: Little Foot
description: A fast breakdown of Little Foot for builders.

hook.text: Ron Clarke spotted four tiny foot bones in a box of South African cave rubble in 1994. Then he dug.

buildup.text: It took 20 years of painstaking excavation to free 'Little Foot' from solid rock—nearly complete, 3.67M years.

discovery.text: The skeleton is an Australopithecus with a grasping big toe, showing it still climbed trees regularly.

twist.text: Little Foot lived at the same time as Lucy's species but in South rather than East Africa—a separate lineage.

climax.text: Two distant populations evolving in parallel show early hominin diversity was greater than we thought.

punchline.text: Four tiny bones launched a 20-year dig.

quiz.question: How long did it take to excavate Little Foot?
